testName: reject 2 from the management canister
why: reject 2 from aaaaa-aa classified as proof that nothing ran, as it is from every other canister

testName: requests nothing on a Codespaces page
why: a *.github.dev host treated as a local replica, so its root key is fetched

testName: refuses more significant fraction digits than the token has
why: excess fraction digits cut off instead of refused with a RangeError

testName: refuses a forged sender
why: the fake replica no longer checks that the sender is the principal of sender_pubkey

testName: never re-sends an update rejected with code 4
why: an update re-sent after any failure, as v3's call retries did: a reject 4 means the canister ran it, and the re-send runs it twice

testName: never re-sends an update to aaaaa-aa after HTTP 429
why: a management call re-sent like any other update, although its outcomes prove nothing about what ran

testName: refuses an update while nobody is signed in
why: an update sent for a caller who is not signed in, instead of refused as unauthenticated before anything is sent

testName: unwraps a lower-case result and rejects its err arm as canister_err
why: a result reply handed back as the variant, so an Err resolves as if the call succeeded

testName: polls the same request again after a lost poll
why: one failed read_state ends an update the IC may still answer as outcome_unknown, as agent.update() does with retryTimes 0

testName: polls for an update whose synchronous answer holds no status for it
why: a synchronous answer whose certificate holds no status for the request fails the update instead of polling for it: the v3 fix (icp-js-core#1330) DECISIONS Q8 keeps a regression test for
replace: if (status === undefined) throw new Error("no status for the request")

testName: stops polling for a read once its signal aborts
why: the wait between two polls ignores the read's signal, so a read whose observer went away keeps polling read_state for up to five minutes

testName: ends the wait to poll again after a failed poll as soon as the read's signal aborts
why: the wait before polling again after a transient read_state failure ignores the read's signal, so a read whose observer went away sits out the whole delay and only then notices

testName: sends no poll for a read whose signal aborted while its call was on the way
why: no check of the read's signal before polling, so a read whose observer went away while its call was being sent still polls read_state and resolves for nobody

testName: on a page whose host the cookie is not trusted for
why: a { name } the client must not resolve sent anyway, to the id an untrusted ic_env cookie names

testName: is the read's whole key for a method without arguments
why: queryKey(c, method) for a method without arguments gives the method prefix, so getQueryData misses what queryOptions(c, method) cached and setQueryData makes a second entry

testName: never shows one principal's data under another's key
why: a query function that reads the caller when it runs instead of using the one captured with its key, so another principal's answer lands under the key
replace:
certified: record.certified,
          caller: internals.current(),
          values,
          encoded,

testName: invalidates the canister's reads after a lost reply
why: a write whose reply was lost leaves the reads it may have changed cached, so the balance shown hides a debit that happened

testName: does not invalidate after a write cancelled before it was sent
why: a write cancelled before anything was sent (its caller signed out) invalidates the canister's reads as if it may have run

testName: invalidates the canister's reads after a success
why: a write invalidates nothing unless invalidates is given (the v4 prototype's default, which DECISIONS Q10 turned down)

testName: invalidates the canister a { name } write went to when the cookie moves the name before the write settles
why: onSettled resolves a { name } from the ic_env cookie again when the write settles, so after a local redeploy mid-write it invalidates the canister the cookie names now and leaves the reads of the one written to stale

testName: keeps a { name } write and its invalidation on one canister when an onMutate of the app's replaces the given one
why: onSettled looks for the run only in what onMutate returned, not by the run's function context, so under an onMutate of the app's that replaces the given one (TanStack's optimistic-update recipe) it resolves a { name } again at settlement, and a local redeploy mid-write leaves the reads of the canister written to stale

testName: sends a { name } write that waited offline to the canister resolved when it started
why: mutationFn resolves a { name } again when it starts instead of using the run onMutate resolved, so a write paused across a local redeploy goes to the new canister while onSettled invalidates the old one's reads

testName: invalidates the canister a { name } in invalidates named when the write started
why: the run keeps the canister it writes to but reads the slots of the canisters listed in invalidates lazily, when the write settles, so a { name } listed there that a local redeploy moves mid-write has the new canister's reads invalidated and the old one's left stale

testName: throws a TypeError for an update or oneway method
why: queryOptions builds a read from an update method, which then runs again on every refetch

testName: throws a TypeError for a method without results
why: queryOptions builds a read of a method without results, whose query function resolves undefined: TanStack Query reports the successful call as a failed read and caches nothing

testName: is fetched once and never refetched on focus, reconnect or remount
why: an update read as a query is refetched when the window regains focus, running the update again

testName: is the target_canister of install_chunked_code
why: install_chunked_code routed by a canister_id field it does not have, instead of its target_canister
